title: When “Better” Prompts Hurt: Evaluation-Driven Iteration for LLM Applications

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating LLM judges in pairwise comparisons to detect systematic preferences for the first or second option presented, mitigated by randomizing presentation order and running comparisons twice.
Measuring the tendency of LLM judges to assign higher ratings to longer responses regardless of actual answer quality, mitigated by explicit rubric criteria or length-normalizing scores.
Assessing whether LLM judges systematically prefer outputs generated by themselves or models from the same family over outputs from other models.
Evaluating the propensity of LLM judges to reward a confident and authoritative tone even when the underlying factual content is incorrect, mitigated by component-level rubric scoring.
